statements.text: We must not aid and abet the Chinese Government's development of advanced technologies—like microchips, 5G, AI, quantum computing, and more—that will shape the course of this century. [...] We must limit investment capital from flowing to the Xi regime—the Chinese Government—and prevent them from taking advantage of America's critical assets.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer previewing a press conference on bipartisan legislation to compete with China, delivered in executive session on May 3, 2023.

statements.text: AI is one of the most pressing and serious policy issues we confront today.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer ahead of a White House meeting with AI company CEOs, outlining a consultative, bipartisan approach to AI policy.

statements.text: If harnessed responsibly, AI has the power to do tremendous things for the public good. It can unlock unimaginable marvels in medicine, business, national security, science, and so many other areas of life; but if left unchecked, AI has the power to do tremendous, tremendous harm.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer spoke on the Senate floor about bipartisan efforts to develop comprehensive AI legislation following a meeting with a bipartisan group of Senators.

statements.text: The first briefing in the next few weeks will focus on the state of artificial intelligence today. [...] The third, our first-ever classified briefing on AI, will focus on how our adversaries will use AI against us, while detailing how defense and intelligence agencies will use this technology to keep Americans safe.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer announces a series of bipartisan all-Senate AI briefings, including a classified national security briefing, on the Senate floor.

statements.text: It is imperative that we Senators take time to educate ourselves on AI and its implications so that we can ensure it becomes a force for human prosperity while mitigating its very real risks.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the chamber during Executive Session to announce a series of all-Senators AI briefings.

statements.text: AI, artificial intelligence, is unlike any innovation that has previously come to the attention of Congress. In a few years, this technology will usher in dramatic changes to the workplace, the classroom, our living rooms—to virtually every corner of life—and it is already starting to happen. Maximizing AI's benefits and mitigating its potential and very real risks will require bipartisan cooperation, focus, and speed from the U.S. Congress.
statements.context: Schumer addresses the Senate floor to announce the first all-Senators AI briefing and urge colleagues to participate.

statements.text: If I had to describe our mindset leaving yesterday's briefing, it was a mix of urgency and humility: urgency because AI is developing so damn fast and humility because AI is stupendously complex.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer following the first all-Senate classified briefing on AI.

statements.text: But we cannot ignore AI's many dangers: AI will dramatically disrupt our workforce, could lead to massive and sophisticated misinformation and weapons, could jaundice our elections and democratic system, and there is the danger that we may prove incapable of managing this technology at all.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the chamber to preview a speech on congressional AI action and outline the need for a bipartisan regulatory framework.

statements.text: Very soon, Mr. President, AI will reshape life on Earth in very dramatic ways. It will transform how we fight disease, tackle hunger, manage our lives, enrich our minds, and ensure peace. But we cannot ignore AI's dangers: workforce disruptions in a very serious way, misinformation and new weapons, threats against our elections, and there is the danger that we may prove incapable of managing this technology at all. Congress cannot behave like ostriches in the sand when it comes to AI.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the chamber on AI policy, introducing his SAFE Innovation framework and announcing expert forums to inform future legislation.

statements.text: We are still in the early stages of understanding AI's role in our national security. So this briefing will be critical for Senators to learn more about how we are using AI to protect our country; also, how it is being used by our adversaries; and what we can do to make sure that we maintain our advantages.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks opening the July work period, in which Majority Leader Schumer announces a classified all-Senators AI briefing from the DOD and intelligence community.

statements.text: Today's classified briefing is crucial because, of all the issues AI would impact, national security may well be the most consequential. [...] In the hands of autocrats or foreign adversaries or domestic rogue actors interested in political chaos or financial gain, the dangers of AI could be extreme.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer announcing classified all-Senate AI briefings and upcoming expert insight forums as part of his SAFE Innovation Framework.

statements.text: Of the many things yesterday's briefing made clear, one of them was that government must play a role in making sure AI works for society's benefit.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the floor after the Senate's first classified AI national-security briefing, outlining next steps for legislative action.

statements.text: But there are real risks too. We must now work to anticipate the risks, mitigate them, and ensure that AI innovation is safe in the decades to come.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer announcing the third all-Senate AI briefing scheduled for July 26, 2023.

statements.text: My AI amendment includes provisions that will boost AI oversight within the national security space, including an increase in data sharing within the DOD, new risk studies to examine explainability and similar issues, and it provides for ``bug bounty programs'' that will help sniff out vulnerability in AI systems used by the DOD.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addressing the floor during executive session on the NDAA, highlighting amendments in the managers' package.

statements.text: Finally, this year's NDAA will take important steps on artificial intelligence. My amendment, which I worked on with Senators Rounds, Young, and Heinrich, will increase data sharing within DOD, increase reporting on AI's use in the financial services industry, create a ``bug bounty program'' where ethical hackers help us find vulnerabilities in our defenses, and much, much more.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer during NDAA FY2024 consideration, highlighting amendments in the managers' package.

statements.text: It shows there is real bipartisan interest in AI, which will be necessary if we want to make progress on what really is imperative for this country: putting together AI legislation that encourages innovation but has safeguards to prevent the liabilities that AI could present.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the floor during NDAA processing, pivoting to recap the Senate's AI briefing series and announce upcoming AI Insight Forums.

statements.text: We are passing the first piece of legislation related to artificial intelligence, including important provisions to increase data sharing with the DOD and increase reporting on AI's use in financial services.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer's floor remarks on the NDAA for Fiscal Year 2024, summarizing bipartisan provisions including AI-related measures.

statements.text: We will, for one, continue laying a foundation for bipartisan congressional action on AI. Next Wednesday, along with Senators Rounds, Heinrich, and Young, I will host the Senate's inaugural AI Insight Forum, a first-ever convening of the top minds in AI here in the Congress.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the chamber at the start of the Senate's return from recess, outlining the legislative agenda including government funding and AI policy.

statements.text: Legislating AI is certainly not going to be easy.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks announcing the inaugural AI Insight Forum series, September 6, 2023.

statements.text: That means both creative innovation to develop new applications, new technologies, new breakthroughs so we can advance in science and in medicine and in education and in health and in so many other areas—communications. But we also need innovation on guardrails so we can find creative and new ways to protect our kids, our privacy, prevent racial bias, prevent doomsday scenarios.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer announcing the first AI Insight Forum and outlining a bipartisan approach to AI policy.

statements.text: But there is also innovation in keeping guardrails, the kind of essential innovation that is needed to prevent AI from going off track, and we might lose it all—and bipartisan because if AI becomes a partisan issue, it will paralyze any chance for progress.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer announcing the first AI Insight Forum on the Senate floor.

statements.text: Tomorrow morning, I will convene, with Senators Rounds and Heinrich and Young, the first of a series of AI Insight Forums to bring leaders from inside and outside the industry to debate Congress's role in regulating AI.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addressing the Senate floor to announce the first AI Insight Forum.

statements.text: First, Congress must play a role—must play a role—in regulating AI. [...] But at the same time and with equal vehemence—maybe even more—we had a consensus on the need for guardrails for a sustainable innovation, because just as AI can be used to design cancer cures, it could also, if things went wrong, be used to make terrible bioweapons or other dangers. [...] I think everyone at the forum agreed that if we don't do anything on AI, then the lowest common denominator can occur: Racial bias that is in our society would be enshrined in AI; massive job displacement and even more unthinkable doomsday scenarios.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer reports on the first bipartisan AI Insight Forum from the Senate floor, summarizing areas of consensus on AI regulation and innovation.

statements.text: AI could be used to jaundice, even totally discredit, our elections as early as next year. [...] Make no mistake, the risks of AI on our elections is not just an issue for Democrats, nor just Republicans.
statements.context: Senator Schumer delivers opening remarks at a Senate Rules Committee hearing on AI and elections.

statements.text: Next week, we will turn to AI innovation, both transformational innovation—the kind of innovation that creates new vistas, unlocks new cures, improves education, protects our food supply and our national security—but also to sustainable innovation, which is the kind of guardrails that are needed to prevent the negatives in AI, necessary to prevent against AI's risks and minimize the chance that this technology becomes unmanageable or worse.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the chamber on the floor, announcing the second bipartisan AI Insight Forum and summarizing congressional AI oversight efforts.

statements.text: We will talk about the need for transformative innovation— the types of AI systems that will create new vistas, unlock new cures, improve education, protect national security, preserve the global food supply, and more. But we will also talk about the need for sustainable innovation—innovations that can solve the deep challenges of AI, like increasing transparency and security, and reducing bias and risk. And this means supporting effective guardrails, because everyone agreed at our last forum, from one end of the spectrum to the other, that if the Federal Government doesn't impose some guardrails, there will be none, and the whole invention of AI could come tumbling down.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer announcing the second bipartisan AI Insight Forum, focused on innovation and guardrails.

statements.text: The biggest takeaway from our AI Insight Forums so far is that government has to be involved on AI, and that was the consensus among everybody yesterday, just as it was a few weeks ago. [...] We need the government to help create innovation, both on the transformational side—creating new vistas, unlocking new cures, improving education, strengthening national security, protecting global food supply—but also, and this is harder, on sustainable innovation. That means to minimize the harms that come from AI like job loss, racial and gender bias, and economic displacement because if we don't have some guardrails, the whole thing, the whole AI enterprise, could go off the rails, and that would be of real detriment to this country and to our world.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addressed the floor about the second bipartisan AI Insight Forum, discussing government investment, competition with China, and the need for regulatory guardrails.

statements.text: I applaud the President for breaking new ground with this Executive order, and I told him that the Senate will work very closely with the White House to do more on AI through legislation.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the floor following President Biden's signing of the first AI Executive Order, outlining next steps for Senate legislative efforts.

statements.text: I applaud President Biden for doing the right thing by issuing yesterday's Executive order. [...] better protect Americans against all sorts of risk, from cyber security to bio and nuclear threats.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer remarks on the Senate floor, praising President Biden's AI executive order and previewing bipartisan AI Insight Forums.

statements.text: People are worried. Many people worry, Will I still have my job as AI kicks in? We want to make sure that we have guardrails that protect workers, not make the mistake that was done with globalization, where so many were thrown out of work through no fault of their own.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the floor on government funding and the Senate's AI Insight Forums, held the same day as the London AI summit.

statements.text: This morning, I will join with colleagues from both sides and with experts from across the country for our AI Insight Forum on elections and democracy. [...] This is the problem we now face: If left unchecked, AI has the potential to erode our democracy from within and from abroad. Political ads have already been released this year using AI-generated images and text-to-voice converters to depict certain candidates in a negative light. Uncensored chatbots can already be deployed in a massive scale to target millions of individual voters for political persuasion. [...] If we don't enact the right guardrails soon, we could soon live in a world where political campaigns regularly deploy totally fabricated yet totally believable images and footage of Democratic or Republican candidates, distorting their statements and greatly harming their election chances.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer ahead of an AI Insight Forum on elections and democracy.

statements.text: AI will be a dramatic force multiplier for the spread of disinformation. [...] We also agreed that government can't alone act to create guardrails to protect our elections in the age of AI.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer reporting on the fifth and sixth bipartisan AI Insight Forums, with a focus on elections and democracy.

statements.text: Our discussion focused on a few of the most critical issues we face with AI: transparency, explainability, intellectual property, and copyright. [...] We must create and enforce protections for creators to maintain their identities in the age of AI. [...] We must protect American companies' IP and make sure America sets the international standard for IP. [...] We must make sure AI systems are transparent and that the public can understand why AI systems produce the answers they do.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the chamber to report on the seventh bipartisan AI Insight Forum.

statements.text: Earlier this summer, the Senate overwhelmingly passed a measure limiting the free flow of U.S. investment into China for sensitive advanced technologies like semiconductors, AI, and more. [...] It would codify elements of an Executive order that President Biden issued in August on outbound investments. [...] What is more commonsense than stopping U.S. dollars from helping Chinese companies beat us on chips and AI and quantum computing?
statements.context: Senate floor remarks during Executive Session on the National Defense Authorization Act, December 4, 2023.

statements.text: Mr. President, now, today, on our AI Insight Forums, we will continue our work with our eighth and ninth bipartisan AI forums. [...] The morning's Insight Forum will begin at 10:30 a.m. and focus on long-term risks associated with AI and how we can guard against AI doomsday scenarios. [...] This afternoon's Insight Forum will begin at 3 p.m. and focus on one of the most critical and urgent areas of AI national security. We will discuss the opportunities AI presents to bolster our national security and the risks if we fall behind the Chinese Government.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer speaks on the Senate floor announcing the eighth and ninth bipartisan AI Insight Forums, covering long-term AI risks and AI national security.

statements.text: Now, on artificial intelligence, as we begin the new year, one of the Senate's top priorities will be to legislate on artificial intelligence.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the chamber on the Senate's AI legislative agenda for 2024.

statements.text: Micron is the leading manufacturer of memory chips, which are critical to everything from cell phones to cars to AI. And this major chips investment is making possible the largest and one of the most advanced memory chip projects in the United States and even in the world, and it is critical to our national security and competitiveness.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer announcing a $6.1 billion CHIPS Act award to Micron for memory chip manufacturing in New York and Idaho.

statements.text: Mr. President, now, on AI, I just returned from the Special Competitive Studies Project's first ever expo on artificial intelligence, where I spoke about the Senate's ongoing efforts to tackle AI.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the floor on legislative priorities including AI, following the Special Competitive Studies Project's AI expo.

statements.text: Our policy roadmap also embraces action to protect our elections from the potential risk of AI. First, the 2024 elections will be the first elections ever held in the age of AI. If we are not careful, AI could jaundice, even totally discredit, our entire system of elections as we know it.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the floor to announce the release of the bipartisan Senate AI policy roadmap and outline committee next steps.

statements.text: So I was pleased that yesterday Chair Peters and Senator Tillis introduced a bipartisan bill to make sure the Federal Government is proactive in harnessing AI's potential while managing its very real risks. [...] This legislation will establish some of the first guidelines for the responsible procurement of AI by the Federal Government.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer during an executive session on artificial intelligence, discussing bipartisan AI procurement legislation and the blocked DEFIANCE Act.

statements.text: First, just now, the Senate unanimously passed a bill to combat the spread of sexually explicit AI-generated deepfakes, the DEFIANCE Act. I commend Senator Durbin for his excellent work on this bill.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer celebrating passage of the DEFIANCE Act and the Preventing Financing of Illegal Synthetic Drugs Act.

statements.text: AI plays a bigger role in our lives than ever before, and while it has many, many benefits, it is also easier than ever to create sexually explicit deepfakes without a person's consent.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer remarks on the floor during a legislative session, highlighting the Senate's passage of the DEFIANCE Act and other bills.

statements.text: We all know AI has many incredible benefits, but alongside those benefits come great risks; and the risks of AI for our elections could be severe. If we are not careful, if we fail to install proper guardrails, AI could jaundice and even totally discredit our entire election system as we know it. Misinformation is already a serious problem in our elections, but AI makes it easier than ever to generate and spread it. It is easier than ever to create deepfakes of candidates.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer urging unanimous consent passage of two election-related AI bills sponsored by Senator Klobuchar.

statements.text: I have always said we need with AI two things: to promote safe innovation, on the one hand, but instill commonsense guardrails, on the other.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer summarizing recent bipartisan AI legislative progress.

statements.text: This award was made possible precisely because of the law I wrote and passed. This chips award is now locked in. The agreement is signed, sealed, and delivered—in fact, ready to deliver a better future for Upstate New York and for America. Importantly, this funding is protected for years to come.
statements.context: Senate floor statement by Majority Leader Schumer announcing a CHIPS Act award to GlobalFoundries.

statements.text: It boosts the use of AI for our national defense—another thing I care a lot about [...] It also includes bipartisan measures on AI to expand our AI infrastructure and strengthen America's edge against the CCP, the Chinese Communist Party, in this critical technology—so important to our national security and to the United States' technological leadership.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer remarks on the Senate floor during a legislative session, discussing NDAA passage and its provisions.

statements.text: Policies to outcompete China, including outsourcing, policies on artificial intelligence, and policies to bring manufacturing back to America, including chip production.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer speaks on the floor about provisions in the continuing resolution and the NDAA, highlighting AI-related measures among many other legislative accomplishments.

statements.text: On AI, yesterday, a group of AI and tech companies announced their pledge to invest as much as $500 billion to ramp up our Nation's AI and data center infrastructure. [...] On the one hand, he goes on about how we need more power, we need more electricity to meet the demands of AI, and then on the other hand, he spent his first day in office proposing Executive orders that cut clean energy investments, halting wind and solar and putting those jobs at risk. [...] So for President Trump to cut clean energy investments is tantamount to cutting AI's potential.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer on January 22, 2025, addressing Trump administration early actions and a major AI infrastructure investment pledge.

statements.text: Today's announcement from China has been called AI's ``Sputnik moment'' for America.
statements.context: Senate Majority Leader Schumer addresses the chamber on the Senate floor regarding the release of DeepSeek's AI model by China.

statements.text: China's innovation with DeepSeek is jarring, but it is nothing compared to what will happen if China beats the United States on the ultimate goal of AGI—artificial general intelligence. [...] This is precisely why I made AI a top priority in the last Congress, with American innovation as my North Star, and I will continue to do so.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Senator Chuck Schumer on January 28, 2025, reacting to the DeepSeek AI announcement and urging congressional action on AI competitiveness.

statements.text: I am alarmed that these deals announced by Donald Trump, which involve the most advanced AI-related semiconductors, have ``national security threat'' written all over them.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Senator Chuck Schumer criticizing the Trump administration's semiconductor export deals with Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

statements.text: This Musk contract is not just wrong, it is not just offensive, it is dangerous. The Trump administration must explain how this happened, the parameters of the deal, and why they think our national security isn't worth meeting a higher standard.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Senator Chuck Schumer criticizing a DOD contract to deploy Elon Musk's Grok AI model in national defense systems after the model generated Nazi and anti-Semitic content.

statements.text: The administration should revert to its original decision, in April, to block the sale of these chips to the Chinese Government. Donald Trump should stop giving the Chinese Government leverage in the race for technologies of the future.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Majority Leader Schumer criticizing the Trump administration's reversal of export controls on Nvidia H20 AI chips sold to China.

statements.text: On the contrary, he is giving the Chinese Government greater access to U.S. semiconductors that are vital— vital—for our national security. [...] By sending them these sophisticated chips, they are going to allow China to catch up to us in things like AI and many other new technological advances. A few years back, we worked hard to see that these vital chips were not sent to China, but in one fell swoop, without any real explanation as to the damage it will do, Donald Trump reversed it.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Senator Chuck Schumer criticizing Trump administration tariff policies and the reversal of semiconductor export controls toward China.

statements.text: Over the past few weeks, Donald Trump has granted the Chinese Government greater access to American advanced AI chips vital to our national security.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Majority Leader Schumer criticizing the Trump administration's China policy, particularly the relaxation of AI chip export controls.

statements.text: vertical corporate integration of neurotechnology, artificial intelligence systems, wearable devices, digital platforms, and global data infrastructure may create interconnected systems with insufficient transparency, accountability, or user control regarding the use of such data; [...] such concentration increases the risk of behavioral influence, cognitive manipulation, erosion of personal autonomy, and the exacerbation of existing social and economic disparities [...] the Commission shall conduct a study on [...] the extent to which existing laws, regulations, and governing frameworks [...] govern the use, storage, processing, portability, and privacy of such data [...] an examination of how the application of artificial intelligence to neural and other related data that can reveal an individual's mental state or activity may reshape the risks, oversight demands, and ethical considerations associated with such data [...]
statements.context: Senator Schumer introduces S. 2925, the MIND Act of 2025, by unanimous consent on the Senate floor, placing the full bill text into the Congressional Record.

statements.text: He is using the most advanced semiconductor chips, which China doesn't have, as a bargaining chip. China is desperate to get these chips. If Trump gives it away, China will dominate the world of AI in a few short years, and Americans will pay an awful price.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Chuck Schumer during a government shutdown, critiquing President Trump's Asia trip and warning against trading away semiconductor export controls in China trade negotiations.

statements.text: he is the first President in decades to walk back export controls that are vital for our national security, essentially handing China vital chips necessary for technologies like AI. [...] With these chips that China now doesn't have and can't make themselves, China will dominate AI in a few years, and it will have severe consequences for America and for the world.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Senator Schumer criticizing Trump's trade deal with China, particularly the rollback of chip export controls.

statements.text: Donald Trump announced he was giving the green light to NVIDIA to send even more powerful AI chips to China—the H200, which are used to train AI models. [...] They will use them to strengthen their military, their technological edge—all at the expense of American and world national security.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Majority Leader Schumer on December 9, 2025, criticizing President Trump's approval of NVIDIA H200 chip sales to China.

statements.text: Donald Trump could sell out America on chips and AI, allowing the sale of our AI chips and semiconductor equipment to China so they can catch up in the technology race that will define the global economy for the next decade. This is a clear and present threat, not just to American jobs but to our national security.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Majority Leader Schumer critiquing Trump administration policies on China, the Federal Reserve, and consumer protections.

statements.text: Trump is continuing to roll forward on selling AI chips to Chinese companies that are linked to the Chinese military. Giving China access to this premiere American technology—something we developed with our know-how, our entrepreneurship, our ingenuity—and just giving it away to China? That is dangerous and threatens the United States' lead in the AI race that is going to shape the global economy for decades.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Chuck Schumer criticizing President Trump's China trip, including AI chip sales and trade negotiations.

statements.text: I urge my colleagues as well to ask Rubio to address recent reports that the Trump administration left a loophole open for the past year and a half that allowed China to acquire, potentially, hundreds of thousands of cutting-edge American AI chips.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Senator Schumer addressing several topics, including urging colleagues to question Secretary Rubio about a reported loophole in AI chip export controls.
